title: Design SQL
summary: Design an in-memory table store: named tables with a fixed number of columns; insertRow appends a row with a table-local increasing id starting at 1 (deleted ids are not reused); deleteRow removes a row; selectCell returns one cell by one-based column index.
inputFormat: A table list with column counts; insertRow takes a table name and row values; deleteRow takes a table name and row id; selectCell takes a table name, row id and one-based column id.
outputFormat: insertRow returns the new row id; selectCell returns the stored string cell value; deleteRow returns nothing.
tieRules: Row ids increase and are never reused.
edgeRules: One-based column indexing (draft). Behaviour on a deleted or missing row is not recorded.

examples.label: authored-reference
examples.input: table with 2 columns: insertRow ['a','b'] -> 1; insertRow ['c','d'] -> 2; selectCell(2,2) -> 'd'; deleteRow(1); insertRow -> 3
examples.note: Conditional on insertRow returning the id, which is not recorded.
